name: AD8475ARMZ-R7
title: AD8475: precision fully differential funnel amplifier, pin-selected gain 0.4 or 0.8, 3 V to 10 V supply
summary: A fully differential amplifier with laser-trimmed internal resistors that attenuates by 0.4 or 0.8, chosen by which input pair is driven. It converts single-ended or differential signals of up to ±10 V into a differential output centred on the VOCM voltage, made to drive 16-bit and 18-bit SAR and other ADCs from one low supply, and its inputs survive ±15 V on a 5 V supply. It runs from 3 V to 10 V single or ±1.5 V to ±5 V dual at 3 mA, with rail-to-rail outputs. A grade comes in a 10-lead MSOP and a 16-lead 3 mm × 3 mm LFCSP; B grade, with tighter gain error, offset and CMRR, comes in the MSOP only.

circuits.title: Typical configuration, 10-lead MSOP
circuits.description: Gain of 0.4 from a single-ended source. A low-impedance source drives +IN 0.4x and -IN 0.4x is grounded; the 0.8x inputs stay open. Each supply has 0.1 µF and 10 µF to ground. VOCM is taken from an external reference and bypassed with 0.1 µF. The output is the difference between +OUT and -OUT. For a gain of 0.8 the ±IN 0.8x pins are driven instead.
notes: VOUT = V+OUT - V-OUT.

circuits.title: Typical configuration, 16-lead LFCSP
circuits.description: The same gain-of-0.4 hookup in the LFCSP. The source drives both +IN 0.4x pins (1 and 16); both -IN 0.4x pins (4 and 5) go to ground. The three +VS pins are tied together and bypassed with 0.1 µF and 10 µF, as are the three -VS pins. VOCM comes from a reference with 0.1 µF to ground.
notes: VOUT = V+OUT - V-OUT.
EPAD is soldered to the ground plane.

circuits.title: Attenuation and level shifting of industrial voltages to drive a single-supply precision ADC
circuits.description: A ±10 V (20 V p-p) ground-referenced signal enters +IN 0.4x with -IN 0.4x grounded; the AD8475 runs at a gain of 0.4 from 5 V with -VS at ground. VOCM sits at 2.5 V from two 10 kΩ resistors across the 5 V reference rail, with 0.1 µF to ground, so each output swings 0.5 V to 4.5 V in antiphase: 8 V p-p differential into the AD7982's IN+ and IN-. Two 20 Ω resistors, 270 pF from each ADC input to ground and 1.3 nF across the inputs form a one-pole filter: 29.5 MHz common mode (20 Ω, 270 pF) and 3.1 MHz differential (40 Ω, 1.3 nF). An ADR435 fed from 7 V to 18 V makes the 5 V rail for the AD8475 supply, the ADC's REF and the divider.
notes: -OUT feeds the ADC's IN- and +OUT its IN+.
Measured result in this circuit: the FFT results table.

circuits.title: AD8475-EVALZ evaluation board
circuits.description: The evaluation board around the LFCSP. SMB inputs IN+ (J1) and IN- (J2) each carry a load position to ground (R5, R6) and reach the 0.4x or 0.8x input pins through 0 Ω links (R2 to pins 1/16, R1 to pin 2, R3 to pin 3, R4 to pins 4/5), so the gain is chosen by which links are fitted. Each output passes a series position (R7, R8) to its SMB (J4 OUT-, J5 OUT+), with positions to ground (R9, R10), across the pair (R12) and a jumper JP1 across the pair. VOCM goes to SMB J3 and a test point with C5 and position R11 to ground. Each supply has 0.1 µF and 10 µF to ground.
notes: R5 to R12 carry no value; they are places for the input and load impedances.
EPAD is soldered to the ground plane.

equations.name: DC transfer of the amplifier
equations.expr: VIN,cm × (RP - RN) + ½ × VIN,dm × (2·RP·RN + RP + RN) = VOUT,cm × (RP - RN) + ½ × VOUT,dm × (2 + RP + RN)

where.RP: RFP / RGP, the ratio of feedback to gain resistor on the side driven by VP
where.RN: RFN / RGN, the same ratio on the side driven by VN

equations.note: Found by superposition on the amplifier with its two feedback networks at one gain.

equations.name: Differential closed-loop gain
equations.expr: VOUT,dm / VIN,dm = (2·RP·RN + RP + RN) / (2 + RP + RN)

equations.name: Common-mode to differential gain
equations.note: A mismatch between the two resistor ratios turns input common-mode voltage into differential output; with RP = RN it is zero.

where.RG: gain resistor, 2.5 kΩ at G = 0.4 or 1.25 kΩ at G = 0.8

equations.name: Voltage at the internal amplifier inputs
equations.expr: VPLUS = VMINUS = RG / (RF + RG) × VOUT,cm + RF / (RF + RG) × VIN,cm
equations.note: For accurate, low-distortion operation this voltage stays below +VS - 1 V and above -VS.

operation.text: A fully differential voltage-feedback amplifier with laser-trimmed on-chip gain and feedback resistors gives fixed attenuations of 0.4 and 0.8. Its two outputs move by equal amounts in opposite directions. One loop, closed through the trimmed resistors, sets the differential output; a second, internal loop holds the output common-mode voltage equal to VOCM. Gain-bandwidth product is nominally constant, the internal summing nodes are high impedance and the outputs low impedance. Output balance holds up well across frequency.

The gain is set by which input pair is driven: ±IN 0.4x for 0.4, ±IN 0.8x for 0.8. In the gain-of-0.4 path the input sees 2.5 kΩ (two 1.25 kΩ in series) into the 1 kΩ feedback; in the 0.8 path it sees 1.25 kΩ.

Gain accuracy and CMRR come mainly from how well the two feedback networks match. The trim guarantees CMRR of at least 86 dB (50 µV/V) and gain error under 0.05%; a discrete build would need resistors matched to 0.01% or better. The resistors' absolute value is held only to ±20%.

Two 200 kΩ resistors inside, one to each supply, bias VOCM to midsupply; left open, it holds the output common mode within 0.01% of midsupply. A different level is set by driving the pin from a source of less than 100 Ω output resistance, and the VOCM gain error figure applies to such a low-impedance drive. An external midsupply divider of two equal resistors can use larger values, because it parallels the internal pair. Because of the internal divider, current flows into or out of the pin according to the applied voltage and the source resistance. Deriving VOCM from the ADC reference through a divider cuts supply noise and centres the outputs in the ADC input range. On a single supply equal to the reference voltage, two 10 kΩ resistors override the internal pair; in other cases a voltage follower drives VOCM.

Drive one input of the chosen pair from the signal and ground the other; no external parts are needed. Driving the other input instead only swaps the output polarity. Fully differential inputs are accepted as well.

The gain and feedback resistors divide the input down before it reaches the internal amplifier, so inputs beyond the supply rails can be measured. The limit is the internal summing-node voltage, which must stay below +VS - 1 V and above -VS; the internal amplifier has rail-to-rail inputs. On a 5 V supply at G = 0.4 a single-ended input up to ±12.5 V keeps full distortion performance.
ESD diodes at the inputs keep the part safe for inputs from -VS - 16 V to +VS + 10.5 V; with 5 V on +VS and ground on -VS that spans ±15 V.

Resistance in the source upsets the resistor ratios and so degrades gain accuracy and CMRR. Drive the inputs from a low-impedance source such as another amplifier; for best performance keep the source impedance under 0.1 Ω.

Single supply 3 V to 10 V or dual supplies ±1.5 V to ±5 V; supply current is 3.2 mA maximum at 25 °C, and a single 5 V supply gives 16 mW of dissipation. Use a stable dc supply, since supply noise degrades performance. Put 0.1 µF from each supply pin to ground as close to the pin as possible, and a 10 µF tantalum from each supply to ground, which may be farther away and shared with other precision parts.

AC and dc performance suit 16-bit and 18-bit SAR converters up to 4 MSPS, and it settles within 18-bit accuracy fast enough for 4 MSPS sampling. The high-current output stage drives switched-capacitor ADC inputs. In the ADC-driver circuit a 20 V p-p ground-referenced input at G = 0.4 on 5 V becomes 8 V p-p differential around 2.5 V; an RC network between amplifier and ADC limits aliasing and high-frequency noise, and VOCM is bypassed and set with 1% resistors.
The LFCSP's exposed pad is soldered to a ground plane.
The AD8475-EVALZ board lets the gain (0.4 or 0.8) and the input and load impedances be fitted by the user, and can take SMB connectors that mate with the PulSAR ADC evaluation kit.
